results.question: What percentage of those at the end of life now choose euthanasia?
results.answer:
There’s no single global percentage, and it depends heavily on what you count—euthanasia, physician-assisted suicide, or “medical aid in dying” (MAID)—and on the country.

In places where it’s legal and reported, completed cases are a **minority of all deaths**, typically **low single digits**:

| Jurisdiction | Latest data | Completed cases | Share of all deaths |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Netherlands (euthanasia + assisted suicide) | 2024 | 9,958 | ~5.8% |
| Canada (MAID; mostly clinician-administered) | 2023 | 15,343 | 4.7% |
| Belgium (euthanasia) | 2023 | ~3,400 | ~3% |
| Oregon, U.S. (self-administered aid in dying) | 2023 | 560 | ~1.4% |
| California, U.S. (self-administered aid in dying) | 2023 | ~1,281 | ~0.4% |
| Spain (euthanasia) | 2023 | ~766 | ~0.2% |

So the practical range in legal jurisdictions is roughly **0.2% to 6% of all deaths**, with the Netherlands at the high end. Globally it’s much lower because most countries prohibit euthanasia.

If you mean **among people who are terminally ill or formally eligible**, the percentage is higher than among all deaths—studies from the Netherlands and Belgium have found roughly **5–15% in some terminal-cancer groups**—but it is still a minority. Also, many people who request it ultimately do not die by euthanasia.

If you tell me which country or state you’re asking about, I can give the exact latest figure.
